questions.questionText: $n$ mole of a perfect gas undergoes a cyclic process ABCA (see figure) consisting of the following processes. A $\to$ B : Isothermal expansion at temperature $T$ so that the volume is doubled from $V_1$ to $V_2 = 2V_1$ and pressure changes from $P_1$ to $P_2$. B $\to$ C : Isobaric compression at pressure $P_2$ to initial volume $V_1$. C $\to$ A : Isochoric change leading to change of pressure from $P_2$ to $P_1$. Total work done in the complete cycle ABCA is :
questions.explanation: A $\to$ B (isothermal): $W_1 = nRT\ln\dfrac{2V_1}{V_1} = nRT\ln 2$. B $\to$ C (isobaric): $W_2 = P_2(V_1 - 2V_1) = -P_2V_1 = -\dfrac{nRT}{2}$ (since $P_2 \cdot 2V_1 = nRT$). C $\to$ A (isochoric): $W_3 = 0$. Hence $W_{net} = nRT\left(\ln 2 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.

questions.questionText: The focal length f is related to the radius of curvature r of the spherical convex mirror by:
questions.explanation: For a spherical mirror the focus lies midway between the pole and the centre of curvature, so $|f| = \dfrac{r}{2}$. For a convex mirror both F and C lie behind the mirror, so with the Cartesian sign convention $f = +\dfrac{r}{2}$.

questions.questionText: In a Young's double slit experiment, the width of the one of the slit is three times the other slit. The amplitude of the light coming from a slit is proportional to the slit-width. Find the ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity in the interference pattern.
questions.explanation: Amplitude $\propto$ slit width, so $A_2 = 3A_1$. Since $I \propto A^2$: $\dfrac{I_{max}}{I_{min}} = \dfrac{(A_1 + A_2)^2}{(A_2 - A_1)^2} = \dfrac{(4A_1)^2}{(2A_1)^2} = \dfrac{4}{1}$, i.e. $4 : 1$.

questions.questionText: Two stars of masses m and 2m at a distance d rotate about their common centre of mass in free space. The period of revolution is :
questions.explanation: The centre of mass is at $d/3$ from mass $2m$ and $2d/3$ from $m$. For mass $2m$: $\dfrac{G(2m)m}{d^2} = (2m)\omega^2\dfrac{d}{3} \Rightarrow \omega^2 = \dfrac{3Gm}{d^3}$. Hence $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{d^3}{3Gm}}$.

questions.questionText: A current through a wire depends on time as $i = \alpha_0 t + \beta t^2$ where $\alpha_0 = 20\ \text{A/s}$ and $\beta = 8\ \text{A s}^{-2}$. Find the charge crossed through a section of the wire in 15 s.

Moment of inertia (M.I.) of four bodies, having same mass and radius, are reported as: $I_1$ = M.I. of thin circular ring about its diameter, $I_2$ = M.I. of circular disc about an axis perpendicular to the disc and going through the centre, $I_3$ = M.I. of solid cylinder about its axis and $I_4$ = M.I. of solid sphere about its diameter. Then :
questions.explanation: Ring about diameter: $I_1 = \dfrac{MR^2}{2}$. Disc about its axis: $I_2 = \dfrac{MR^2}{2}$. Solid cylinder about its axis: $I_3 = \dfrac{MR^2}{2}$. Solid sphere about diameter: $I_4 = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$. Hence $I_1 = I_2 = I_3 > I_4$.

questions.questionText: Given below are two statements : Statement-I : Two photons having equal linear momenta have equal wavelengths. Statement-II : If the wavelength of photon is decreased, then the momentum and energy of a photon will also decrease. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.explanation: For a photon $p = \dfrac{h}{\lambda}$ and $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$. Equal momenta therefore mean equal wavelengths, so Statement I is true. Decreasing $\lambda$ increases both $p$ and $E$, so Statement II is false.

questions.questionText: In the given figure, a mass $M$ is attached to a horizontal spring which is fixed on one side to a rigid support. The spring constant of the spring is $k$. The mass oscillates on a frictionless surface with time period $T$ and amplitude $A$. When the mass is in equilibrium position, as shown in the figure, another mass $m$ is gently fixed upon it. The new amplitude of oscillation will be :
questions.explanation: At the mean position momentum is conserved when $m$ is placed: $MA\omega = (M+m)A'\omega'$ with $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{M}}$ and $\omega' = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{M+m}}$. So $MA\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{M}} = (M+m)A'\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{M+m}} \Rightarrow A' = A\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{M+m}}$.

questions.questionText: If $Y$, $K$ and $\eta$ are the values of Young's modulus, bulk modulus and modulus of rigidity of any material respectively. Choose the correct relation for these parameters.
questions.explanation: $Y = 3K(1-2\sigma)$ and $Y = 2\eta(1+\sigma)$. Eliminating $\sigma$: $\sigma = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1-\dfrac{Y}{3K}\right) = \dfrac{Y}{2\eta} - 1$, which gives $Y = \dfrac{9K\eta}{3K+\eta}$. Rearranging, $K(9\eta - 3Y) = Y\eta \Rightarrow K = \dfrac{Y\eta}{9\eta - 3Y}$.

questions.questionText: In the given figure, the energy levels of hydrogen atom have been shown along with some transitions marked A, B, C, D and E. The transitions A, B and C respectively represent :

options.text: The ionization potential of hydrogen, second member of Balmer series and third member of Paschen series.
The first member of the Lyman series, third member of Balmer series and second member of Paschen series.
The series limit of Lyman series, third member of Balmer series and second member of Paschen series.
The series limit of Lyman series, second member of Balmer series and second member of Paschen series.

questions.explanation: A: continuum ($n=\infty$) $\to n=1$, the series limit of the Lyman series. B: $n=5 \to n=2$, the third member of the Balmer series ($3\to2$, $4\to2$, $5\to2$). C: $n=5 \to n=3$, the second member of the Paschen series.

questions.questionText: Four identical particles of equal masses 1kg made to move along the circumference of a circle of radius 1 m under the action of their own mutual gravitational attraction. The speed of each particle will be :
questions.explanation: The particles sit at the corners of a square inscribed in the circle. Net force towards the centre on one particle: $F = \dfrac{Gm^2}{(2R)^2} + 2\cdot\dfrac{Gm^2}{(\sqrt{2}R)^2}\cos 45^\circ = \dfrac{Gm^2}{4R^2}\left(1+2\sqrt{2}\right)$. Setting $F = \dfrac{mv^2}{R}$ with $m = 1$ kg, $R = 1$ m: $v = \dfrac{\sqrt{(1+2\sqrt{2})G}}{2}$.

questions.questionText: If the velocity-time graph has the shape AMB, what would be the shape of the corresponding acceleration-time graph ?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the slope of the $v$-$t$ graph. From A to M the graph is a straight line with constant negative slope, and from M to B a straight line with constant positive slope. So $a$ is a negative constant up to M and then a positive constant: graph (2).

questions.questionText: Two equal capacitors are first connected in series and then in parallel. The ratio of the equivalent capacities in the two cases will be:
questions.explanation: Series: $\dfrac{1}{C_s} = \dfrac{1}{C} + \dfrac{1}{C} \Rightarrow C_s = \dfrac{C}{2}$. Parallel: $C_p = C + C = 2C$. Ratio $\dfrac{C_s}{C_p} = \dfrac{C/2}{2C} = \dfrac{1}{4}$, i.e. $1 : 4$.

questions.questionText: If an emitter current is changed by 4 mA, the collector current changes by 3.5 mA. The value of $\beta$ will be :
questions.explanation: $I_E = I_C + I_B \Rightarrow \Delta I_B = \Delta I_E - \Delta I_C = 4 - 3.5 = 0.5$ mA. $\beta = \dfrac{\Delta I_C}{\Delta I_B} = \dfrac{3.5}{0.5} = 7$.

questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II :

List-I
(a) Isothermal
(b) Isochoric
(c) Adiabatic
(d) Isobaric

List-II
(i) Pressure constant
(ii) Temperature constant
(iii) Volume constant
(iv) Heat content is constant

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Isothermal: temperature constant (a $\to$ ii). Isochoric: volume constant (b $\to$ iii). Adiabatic: $\Delta Q = 0$, heat content constant (c $\to$ iv). Isobaric: pressure constant (d $\to$ i).

questions.questionText: Each side of a box made of metal sheet in cubic shape is '$a$' at room temperature '$T$', the coefficient of linear expansion of the metal sheet is '$\alpha$'. The metal sheet is heated uniformly, by a small temperature $\Delta T$, so that its new temperature is $T + \Delta T$. Calculate the increase in the volume of the metal box.
questions.explanation: Volume expansion coefficient $\gamma = 3\alpha$. So $\Delta V = V\gamma\Delta T = a^3 (3\alpha)\Delta T = 3a^3\alpha\Delta T$.

questions.questionText: A cell $E_1$ of emf 6 V and internal resistance $2\ \Omega$ is connected with another cell $E_2$ of emf 4 V and internal resistance $8\ \Omega$ (as shown in the figure). The potential difference across points X and Y is :
questions.explanation: The cells oppose each other, so $I = \dfrac{6-4}{2+8} = 0.2$ A, flowing in the direction set by $E_1$ (so $E_2$ is being charged). P and Y are joined by a wire, so $|V_X - V_Y| = |V_X - V_P| = E_1 - Ir_1 = 6 - 0.2 \times 2 = 5.6$ V (equivalently $E_2 + Ir_2 = 4 + 1.6 = 5.6$ V).

questions.questionText: A cube of side '$a$' has point charges $+Q$ located at each of its vertices except at the origin where the charge is $-Q$. The electric field at the centre of cube is :
questions.explanation: Replace $-Q$ at the origin by $+Q$ and $-2Q$. Eight $+Q$ charges give zero field at the centre, so only $-2Q$ at the origin contributes. The centre is at $\vec{r} = \dfrac{a}{2}(\hat{x}+\hat{y}+\hat{z})$, $|\vec{r}| = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}a}{2}$. $\vec{E} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{(-2Q)\vec{r}}{r^3} = \dfrac{-2Q}{3\sqrt{3}\pi\epsilon_0 a^2}(\hat{x}+\hat{y}+\hat{z})$.

questions.questionText: Consider two satellites $S_1$ and $S_2$ with periods of revolution $1\text{ hr}$ and $8\text{ hr}$ respectively revolving around a planet in circular orbits. The ratio of angular velocity of satellite $S_1$ to the angular velocity of satellite $S_2$ is :
questions.explanation: $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$, so $\dfrac{\omega_1}{\omega_2} = \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = \dfrac{8}{1}$, i.e. $8 : 1$.

questions.questionText: The work done by a gas molecule in an isolated system is given by, $W = \alpha\beta^2 e^{-\frac{x^2}{\alpha kT}}$, where $x$ is the displacement, $k$ is the Boltzmann constant and $T$ is the temperature, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants. Then the dimension of $\beta$ will be :
questions.explanation: The exponent $\dfrac{x^2}{\alpha kT}$ is dimensionless, so $[\alpha] = \dfrac{[x^2]}{[kT]} = \dfrac{\text{L}^2}{\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}} = \text{M}^{-1}\text{T}^2$. Then $[\beta]^2 = \dfrac{[W]}{[\alpha]} = \dfrac{\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}}{\text{M}^{-1}\text{T}^2} = \text{M}^2\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-4}$, so $[\beta] = [\text{M}\,\text{L}\,\text{T}^{-2}]$.

questions.questionText: The coefficient of static friction between a wooden block of mass 0.5 kg and a vertical rough wall is 0.2. The magnitude of horizontal force that should be applied on the block to keep it adhere to the wall will be ______ N. [$g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$]
questions.explanation: The horizontal force $F$ provides the normal reaction $N = F$. For the block not to slip, limiting friction must balance weight: $\mu F = mg \Rightarrow F = \dfrac{mg}{\mu} = \dfrac{0.5 \times 10}{0.2} = 25$ N.

questions.questionText: A resonance circuit having inductance and resistance $2 \times 10^{-4}$ H and $6.28\ \Omega$ respectively oscillates at 10 MHz frequency. The value of quality factor of this resonator is _______. [$\pi = 3.14$]
questions.explanation: $Q = \dfrac{\omega_0 L}{R} = \dfrac{2\pi f L}{R} = \dfrac{2 \times 3.14 \times 10^7 \times 2 \times 10^{-4}}{6.28} = 2000$.

questions.questionText: A hydraulic press can lift 100 kg when a mass 'm' is placed on the smaller piston. It can lift _______kg when the diameter of the larger piston is increased by 4 times and that of the smaller piston is decreased by 4 times keeping the same mass 'm' on the smaller piston.
questions.explanation: By Pascal's law, $\dfrac{mg}{A_1} = \dfrac{100g}{A_2}$. Area $\propto d^2$, so increasing the larger diameter 4 times makes its area $16A_2$ and decreasing the smaller diameter 4 times makes its area $A_1/16$. Then $\dfrac{mg}{A_1/16} = \dfrac{Mg}{16A_2} \Rightarrow M = 256 \times 100 = 25600$ kg.

questions.questionText: An inclined plane is bent in such a way that the vertical cross-section is given by $y = \dfrac{x^2}{4}$ where $y$ is in vertical and $x$ in horizontal direction. If the upper surface of this curved plane is rough with coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.5$, the maximum height in cm at which a stationary block will not slip downward is ________ cm.
questions.explanation: The block stays at rest as long as the slope $\tan\theta \le \mu$. At the maximum height $\tan\theta = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{2} = 0.5 \Rightarrow x = 1$ m, so $y = \dfrac{1^2}{4} = 0.25$ m $= 25$ cm (taking $x$, $y$ in metres).

questions.questionText: An electromagnetic wave of frequency $f = 5\text{ GHz}$ propagates in a medium with relative permittivity $\epsilon_r = 2$ and relative permeability $\mu_r = 2$. If the speed of light in the medium is $x \times 10^7\text{ m/s}$, the value of $x$ is:
questions.explanation: Given $f = 5\text{ GHz}$, $\epsilon_r = 2$, $\mu_r = 2$. Speed of wave in medium is $v = \frac{c}{\sqrt{\epsilon_r \mu_r}} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{\sqrt{2 \times 2}} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{2} = 1.5 \times 10^8\text{ m/s} = 15 \times 10^7\text{ m/s}$. Hence, $x = 15$.

questions.questionText: In connection with the circuit drawn below, the value of current flowing through $2\ \text{k}\Omega$ resistor is ________ $\times 10^{-4}$ A.
questions.explanation: Without the Zener, the voltage across $2\ \text{k}\Omega$ would be $10 \times \dfrac{2}{3} \approx 6.7$ V $> 5$ V, so the Zener breaks down and holds 5 V across the $2\ \text{k}\Omega$ resistor. $I = \dfrac{5}{2 \times 10^3} = 2.5 \times 10^{-3}$ A $= 25 \times 10^{-4}$ A.

questions.questionText: An audio signal $v_m = 20 \sin 2\pi(1500t)$ amplitude modulates a carrier $v_c = 80 \sin 2\pi(100{,}000t)$. The value of percent modulation is _______.
questions.explanation: Percent modulation $= \dfrac{A_m}{A_c} \times 100 = \dfrac{20}{80} \times 100 = 25$.

questions.questionText: A ball with a speed of 9 m/s collides with another identical ball at rest. After the collision, the direction of each ball makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the original direction. The ratio of velocities of the balls after collision is $x : y$, where $x$ is ________.
questions.explanation: Momentum perpendicular to the original direction is initially zero: $mv_1\sin 30^\circ - mv_2\sin 30^\circ = 0 \Rightarrow v_1 = v_2$. So the ratio is $1 : 1$ and $x = 1$.

questions.questionText: A common transistor radio set requires 12 V (D.C.) for its operation. The D.C. source is constructed by using a transformer and a rectifier circuit, which are operated at 220 V (A.C.) on standard domestic A.C. supply. The number of turns of secondary coil are 24, then the number of turns of primary are _______.
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{N_P}{N_S} = \dfrac{V_P}{V_S} \Rightarrow N_P = 24 \times \dfrac{220}{12} = 440$.

questions.questionText: An unpolarized light beam is incident on the polarizer of a polarization experiment and the intensity of light beam emerging from the analyzer is measured as 100 Lumens. Now, if the analyzer is rotated around the horizontal axis (direction of light) by $30^\circ$ in clockwise direction, the intensity of emerging light will be _______ Lumens.
questions.explanation: Taking the polarizer and analyzer axes initially parallel, $\dfrac{I_0}{2} = 100$ lumens. After rotating by $30^\circ$, by Malus' law $I = \dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos^2 30^\circ = 100 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = 75$ lumens.

questions.questionText: The product formed in the first step of the reaction of $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\underset{\text{Br}}{\underset{|}{\text{CH}}}-\text{CH}_2-\underset{\text{Br}}{\underset{|}{\text{CH}}}-\text{CH}_3$ (2,4-dibromohexane) with excess $\text{Mg}/\text{Et}_2\text{O}$ ($\text{Et} = \text{C}_2\text{H}_5$) is :

options.text: Head-to-tail cyclic dimer: 1,4-diethyl-2,5-dimethylcyclohexane (two hexane chains joined at C-3/C-5 of one and C-5/C-3 of the other)
Head-to-head cyclic dimer: 1,2-diethyl-4,5-dimethylcyclohexane (two hexane chains joined C-3 to C-3 and C-5 to C-5)

questions.explanation: With excess Mg in dry ether, each C–Br bond is converted into a C–MgBr bond. So the first-step product is the di-Grignard reagent $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(MgBr)CH}_2\text{CH(MgBr)CH}_3$. (Intramolecular coupling to the cyclopropane would only be a later step.)

questions.questionText: Consider the elements Mg. Al, S, P and Si, the correct increasing order of their first ionization enthalpy is :
questions.explanation: Across a period ionisation enthalpy generally increases, but Mg ($3s^2$, fully filled) has higher IE than Al ($3s^2 3p^1$), and P ($3p^3$, half-filled) has higher IE than S ($3p^4$). Hence the order is Al < Mg < Si < S < P.

questions.questionText: 'A' and 'B' in the following reactions are : $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} \text{(A)} \xrightarrow{\text{SnCl}_2/\text{HCl}/\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{(B)}$
questions.explanation: Aniline is diazotised by $\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}$ (0–5 °C) to benzenediazonium chloride, which with cyanide gives benzonitrile (A). Stephen reduction ($\text{SnCl}_2/\text{HCl}$, then $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$) converts the nitrile into benzaldehyde (B).

questions.questionText: Which of the following ore is concentrated using group 1 cyanide salt ?
questions.explanation: Sphalerite is ZnS, calamine $\text{ZnCO}_3$, siderite $\text{FeCO}_3$, malachite $\text{Cu(OH)}_2\cdot\text{CuCO}_3$. In froth flotation of an ore containing ZnS and PbS, NaCN (a group 1 cyanide) is used as a depressant for ZnS, so sphalerite is the ore handled with cyanide.

questions.questionText: Al2O3 was leached with alkali to get X. The solution of X on passing of gas Y, forms Z. X, Y and Z respectively are :

options.text: X = Na[Al(OH)4], Y = SO2, Z = Al2O3
X = Na[Al(OH)4], Y = CO2, Z = Al2O3.xH2O
X = Al(OH)3, Y = CO2, Z = Al2O3
X = Al(OH)3, Y = SO2, Z = Al2O3.xH2O

questions.explanation: $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \to 2\text{Na[Al(OH)}_4]$ (X). Passing $\text{CO}_2$ (Y) precipitates hydrated alumina: $2\text{Na[Al(OH)}_4] + 2\text{CO}_2 \to \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{NaHCO}_3$ (Z = $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$).

questions.questionText:
Which of the following are isostructural pairs ?
A. $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ and $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$
B. $\text{SiCl}_4$ and $\text{TiCl}_4$
C. $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{NO}_3^-$
D. $\text{BCl}_3$ and $\text{BrCl}_3$
questions.explanation: $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ and $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$ are both tetrahedral; $\text{SiCl}_4$ and $\text{TiCl}_4$ are both tetrahedral. $\text{NH}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal but $\text{NO}_3^-$ is trigonal planar; $\text{BCl}_3$ is trigonal planar but $\text{BrCl}_3$ is T-shaped. Hence A and B only.

questions.questionText:
What is the final product (major) 'A' in the given reaction ?
$\text{CH}_3-\underset{\text{OH}}{\underset{|}{\text{CH}}}-\underset{\text{CH}_3}{\underset{|}{\text{CH}}}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{HCl}} \text{'A'}$ (major product)
questions.explanation: Protonation of –OH and loss of water gives a secondary carbocation $\text{CH}_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$. A 1,2-hydride shift gives the more stable tertiary carbocation $(\text{CH}_3)_2\overset{+}{\text{C}}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which is captured by $\text{Cl}^-$ to give 2-chloro-2-methylbutane.

questions.questionText:
In the following reaction the reason why meta-nitro product also formed is :
Aniline $\xrightarrow[\text{Conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4,\ 288\text{ K}]{\text{Conc. HNO}_3}$ p-nitroaniline [A] (51%) + m-nitroaniline [B] (47%) + o-nitroaniline [C] (2%)

options.text: $-\text{NO}_2$ substitution always takes place at meta-position

questions.explanation: In the strongly acidic nitrating mixture, aniline is protonated to the anilinium ion $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_3^+$, whose $-\text{NH}_3^+$ group is strongly electron-withdrawing ($-I$) and meta-directing. Hence a considerable amount (47%) of m-nitroaniline is formed.

questions.questionText: In Freundlich adsorption isotherm, slope of AB line is :
questions.explanation: Freundlich isotherm: $\dfrac{x}{m} = kP^{1/n}$, so $\log\dfrac{x}{m} = \log k + \dfrac{1}{n}\log P$. A plot of $\log\dfrac{x}{m}$ vs $\log P$ is a straight line of slope $\dfrac{1}{n}$, with $0 \le \dfrac{1}{n} \le 1$.

questions.questionText:
(A) $\text{HOCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \to \text{H}_3\text{O}^+ + \text{Cl}^- + \text{O}_2$
(B) $\text{I}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- \to 2\text{I}^- + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{O}_2$
Choose the correct option.

options.text: $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ acts as reducing and oxidising agent respectively in equation (A) and (B)
$\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ acts as oxidising agent in equation (A) and (B)
$\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ acts as reducing agent in equation (A) and (B)
$\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ act as oxidizing and reducing agent respectively in equation (A) and (B)

questions.explanation: In (A) chlorine is reduced from +1 (HOCl) to −1 ($\text{Cl}^-$) and in (B) iodine is reduced from 0 to −1, while in both $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is oxidised to $\text{O}_2$. So $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ acts as a reducing agent in both.

questions.questionText: What is the major product formed by $\text{HI}$ on reaction with $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$ ?
questions.explanation: HI adds by Markovnikov's rule: $\text{H}^+$ adds to C-3 giving the tertiary carbocation $(\text{CH}_3)_2\overset{+}{\text{C}}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which is attacked by $\text{I}^-$ to give 2-iodo-2-methylpentane.

questions.questionText: Which of the following reagent is used for the reaction : $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3 \to \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$ ?

options.text: Copper at high temperature and pressure

questions.explanation: Controlled oxidation of alkanes with $\text{O}_2$ over molybdenum oxide ($\text{Mo}_2\text{O}_3$) catalyst gives aldehydes, e.g. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \to \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$.

questions.questionText: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Colourless cupric metaborate is reduced to cuprous metaborate in a luminous flame. Statement II : Cuprous metaborate is obtained by heating boric anhydride and copper sulphate in a non-luminous flame. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.explanation: Statement I is false: cupric metaborate is blue, and it is reduced to colourless cuprous metaborate in the luminous flame ($2\text{Cu(BO}_2)_2 + 2\text{NaBO}_2 + \text{C} \to 2\text{CuBO}_2 + \text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 + \text{CO}$). Statement II is false: heating $\text{CuSO}_4$ with $\text{B}_2\text{O}_3$ in a non-luminous flame gives cupric metaborate, $\text{CuSO}_4 + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 \to \text{Cu(BO}_2)_2 + \text{SO}_3$. Hence both statements are false.

questions.questionText: Out of the following, which type of interaction is responsible for the stabilisation of $\alpha$-helix structure of proteins ?
questions.explanation: The $\alpha$-helix is stabilised by intramolecular hydrogen bonds between the $>\text{C}=\text{O}$ of one amino-acid residue and the $-\text{NH}$ of the fourth residue along the chain.

questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II.
List I (Monomer Unit) : (a) Caprolactam (b) 2-Chloro-1,3-butadiene (c) Isoprene (d) Acrylonitrile
List II (Polymer) : (i) Natural rubber (ii) Buna-N (iii) Nylon 6 (iv) Neoprene
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Caprolactam is the monomer of Nylon 6; 2-chloro-1,3-butadiene (chloroprene) gives neoprene; isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene) gives natural rubber; acrylonitrile ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CN}$) with 1,3-butadiene gives Buna-N. So (a)–(iii), (b)–(iv), (c)–(i), (d)–(ii).

questions.questionText: The gas released during anaerobic degradation of vegetation may lead to :
questions.explanation: The gas CH4 evolved due to anaerobic degradation of vegetation which causes global warming and cancer.

questions.questionText: The major components in "Gun Metal" are :
questions.explanation: The major components in "Gun Metal" are Cu : 87% Zn : 3% Sn : 10%

questions.questionText: The electrode potential of $\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}$ of 3d-series elements shows positive value of :
questions.explanation: Among 3d elements only copper has a positive standard reduction potential: $E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}) = +0.34$ V; Zn, Fe and Co have negative values.

questions.questionText: Identify products $A$ and $B$ in the sequence : toluene $\xrightarrow[273\text{ K}]{\text{dil. }\text{KMnO}_4} A \xrightarrow{\text{CrO}_3} B$ :
questions.explanation: dil.KMnO4 273 K HO OH CrO3 OH O (A) Ans. (2) 6

questions.questionText: Which of the following compound gives pink colour on reaction with phthalic anhydride in conc. H2SO4 followed by treatment with NaOH ?
questions.explanation: Phthalic anhydride condenses with two molecules of a phenol (electrophilic substitution para to –OH, conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) to form a phthalein dye, which turns pink in NaOH (as phenol gives phenolphthalein). A phenol needs a free position para to –OH for this reaction.

questions.questionText: When 9.45 g of $\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOH}$ is added to 500 mL of water, its freezing point drops by 0.5$^\circ\text{C}$. The dissociation constant of $\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOH}$ is $x \times 10^{-3}$. The value of $x$ is ________. (Rounded off to the nearest integer) $[K_{f(\text{H}_2\text{O})} = 1.86 \text{ K kg mol}^{-1}]$
questions.explanation: Moles = 9.45/94.5 = 0.1, molality $m = 0.2$. $\Delta T_f = i K_f m \Rightarrow 0.5 = i(1.86)(0.2) \Rightarrow i = 1.344$, so $\alpha = 0.344$. With $C = 0.2$ M, $K_a = \dfrac{C\alpha^2}{1-\alpha} = \dfrac{0.2(0.344)^2}{0.656} \approx 0.036 = 36 \times 10^{-3}$.

questions.questionText: $4.5\text{ g}$ of compound $A$ ($\text{MW} = 90$) was used to make $250\text{ mL}$ of its aqueous solution. The molarity of the solution in $\text{M}$ is $x \times 10^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is _______ (Rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation: Molarity $M = \frac{4.5 / 90}{250 / 1000} = 0.2\text{ M} = 2 \times 10^{-1}\text{ M} \implies x = 2$.

questions.questionText: At 1990 K and 1 atm pressure, there are equal number of $\text{Cl}_2$ molecules and Cl atoms in the reaction mixture. The value of $K_P$ for the reaction $\text{Cl}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{Cl}_{(g)}$ under the above conditions is $x \times 10^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is _______. (Rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation: Equal moles of $\text{Cl}_2$ and Cl at total pressure 1 atm give $p_{\text{Cl}_2} = p_{\text{Cl}} = 0.5$ atm. $K_P = \dfrac{(0.5)^2}{0.5} = 0.5 = 5 \times 10^{-1}$, so $x = 5$.

questions.questionText: Number of amphoteric compound among the following is __________ (A) BeO (B) BaO (C) Be(OH)2 (D) Sr(OH)2
questions.explanation: Both compounds BeO and Be(OH)2 are amphoteric in nature. and both compounds BaO and Sr(OH)2 are basic in nature.

questions.questionText: The reaction of sulphur in alkaline medium is given below : $\text{S}_{8(s)} + a\,\text{OH}^-_{(aq)} \to b\,\text{S}^{2-}_{(aq)} + c\,\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}{}_{(aq)} + d\,\text{H}_2\text{O}_{(l)}$. The value of '$a$' is _______. (Integer answer)
questions.explanation: Reduction: $\text{S}_8 + 16e^- \to 8\text{S}^{2-}$. Oxidation: $\text{S}_8 \to 4\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} + 16e^-$. Adding and balancing O and H with $\text{OH}^-$/$\text{H}_2\text{O}$: $2\text{S}_8 + 24\text{OH}^- \to 8\text{S}^{2-} + 4\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} + 12\text{H}_2\text{O}$, i.e. $\text{S}_8 + 12\text{OH}^- \to 4\text{S}^{2-} + 2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$. So $a = 12$.

questions.questionText: For the reaction $\text{A}_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{B}_{(g)}$, the value of the equilibrium constant at 300 K and 1 atm is equal to 100.0. The value of $\Delta_r G^\circ$ for the reaction at 300 K and 1 atm in J mol$^{-1}$ is $-xR$, where $x$ is ______ (Rounded off to the nearest integer) ($R = 8.31$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ and $\ln 10 = 2.3$)

A proton and a $\text{Li}^{3+}$ nucleus are accelerated by the same potential. If $\lambda_{\text{Li}}$ and $\lambda_{\text{P}}$ denote the de Broglie wavelengths of $\text{Li}^{3+}$ and proton respectively, then the value of $\dfrac{\lambda_{\text{Li}}}{\lambda_{\text{P}}}$ is $x \times 10^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is ________. (Rounded off to the nearest integer) (Mass of $\text{Li}^{3+}$ = 8.3 mass of proton)
questions.explanation: $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$, so $\dfrac{\lambda_{\text{Li}}}{\lambda_{\text{P}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m_p e}{(8.3m_p)(3e)}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{24.9}} \approx 0.2 = 2 \times 10^{-1}$. So $x = 2$.

questions.questionText:
The stepwise formation of $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ is given below :
$\text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{NH}_3 \overset{K_1}{\rightleftharpoons} [\text{Cu(NH}_3)]^{2+}$
$[\text{Cu(NH}_3)]^{2+} + \text{NH}_3 \overset{K_2}{\rightleftharpoons} [\text{Cu(NH}_3)_2]^{2+}$
$[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_2]^{2+} + \text{NH}_3 \overset{K_3}{\rightleftharpoons} [\text{Cu(NH}_3)_3]^{2+}$
$[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_3]^{2+} + \text{NH}_3 \overset{K_4}{\rightleftharpoons} [\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$
The value of stability constants $K_1$, $K_2$, $K_3$ and $K_4$ are $10^4$, $1.58 \times 10^3$, $5 \times 10^2$ and $10^2$ respectively. The overall equilibrium constant for dissociation of $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ is $x \times 10^{-12}$. The value of $x$ is ________. (Rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation: Overall formation constant $K = K_1K_2K_3K_4 = 10^4 \times 1.58 \times 10^3 \times 5 \times 10^2 \times 10^2 = 7.9 \times 10^{11}$. Dissociation constant $= 1/K = 1.27 \times 10^{-12}$, so $x \approx 1$.

questions.questionText: The coordination number of an atom in a body- centered cubic structure is _______. [Assume that the lattice is made up of atoms.]

Gaseous cyclobutene isomerizes to butadiene in a first order process which has a 'k' value of $3.3 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ at 153$^\circ\text{C}$. The time in minutes it takes for the isomerization to proceed 40% to completion at this temperature is _____. (Rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation: For first order, $kt = \ln\dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t} = \ln\dfrac{100}{60} = 0.511$. $t = \dfrac{0.511}{3.3 \times 10^{-4}} \approx 1548$ s $\approx 25.8$ min $\approx 26$ min.

questions.questionText: The statement among the following that is a tautology is:
questions.explanation: $[A \land (A \rightarrow B)] \rightarrow B \equiv [A \land (\sim A \lor B)] \rightarrow B \equiv [(A \land \sim A) \lor (A \land B)] \rightarrow B \equiv (A \land B) \rightarrow B \equiv \sim(A \land B) \lor B \equiv \sim A \lor \sim B \lor B \equiv \text{Tautology (T)}.$

questions.questionText: A man is walking on a straight line. The arithmetic mean of the reciprocals of the intercepts of this line on the coordinate axes is $\frac{1}{4}$. Three stones $A, B$ and $C$ are placed at the points $(1,1)$, $(2, 2)$ and $(4, 4)$ respectively. Then which of these stones is / are on the path of the man ?
questions.explanation: Let the line be $\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1$. The arithmetic mean of reciprocals of intercepts is $\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b}\right) = \frac{1}{4} \implies \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \frac{2}{a} + \frac{2}{b} = 1$. Comparing with $\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1$, the line always passes through $(2, 2)$, which is point $B$.

questions.questionText: The equation of the plane passing through the point $(1, 2, -3)$ and perpendicular to the planes $3x + y - 2z = 5$ and $2x - 5y - z = 7$ is :
questions.explanation: The normal of the required plane is $\vec n_1 \times \vec n_2 = (3\hat i + \hat j - 2\hat k) \times (2\hat i - 5\hat j - \hat k) = -11\hat i - \hat j - 17\hat k$, so its direction ratios are $\langle 11, 1, 17\rangle$. Plane through $(1, 2, -3)$: $11(x-1) + (y-2) + 17(z+3) = 0 \Rightarrow 11x + y + 17z + 38 = 0$.

questions.questionText: The population $P = P(t)$ at time '$t$' of a certain species follows the differential equation $\frac{dP}{dt} = 0.5P - 450$. If $P(0) = 850$, then the time at which population becomes zero is :
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dP}{dt} = \dfrac{P - 900}{2} \Rightarrow \displaystyle\int \dfrac{dP}{P - 900} = \int \dfrac{dt}{2} \Rightarrow \ln|P - 900| = \dfrac{t}{2} + \ln|P(0) - 900| = \dfrac{t}{2} + \ln 50$. For $P(t) = 0$: $\ln 900 - \ln 50 = \dfrac{t}{2} \Rightarrow t = 2\ln 18$.

questions.questionText:
The system of linear equations:
$$\begin{aligned} 3x - 2y - kz &= 10 \\ 2x - 4y - 2z &= 6 \\ x + 2y - z &= 5m \end{aligned}$$
is inconsistent if :
questions.explanation: $\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & -2 & -k \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = 24 - 8k = 0 \Rightarrow k = 3$. With $k = 3$: $\Delta_x = \begin{vmatrix} 10 & -2 & -3 \\ 6 & -4 & -2 \\ 5m & 2 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = 8(4 - 5m)$, $\Delta_y = 0$, $\Delta_z = 8(5m - 4)$. The system is inconsistent when $\Delta = 0$ and some $\Delta_i \neq 0$, i.e. $k = 3,\ m \neq \dfrac{4}{5}$.

questions.questionText: If $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a function defined by $f(x) = [x - 1]\cos\left(\frac{2x - 1}{2}\pi\right)$, where $[.]$ denotes the greatest integer function, then $f$ is :
questions.explanation: Only integer points can be doubtful (where $[x-1]$ jumps). At $x = n \in \mathbb{Z}$, $\cos\left(\dfrac{(2n-1)\pi}{2}\right) = 0$, so LHL $=$ RHL $= f(n) = 0$ (the bounded jump of $[x-1]$ is multiplied by a factor tending to 0). Hence $f$ is continuous for every real $x$.

questions.questionText: The distance of the point $(1, 1, 9)$ from the point of intersection of the line $\frac{x-3}{1} = \frac{y-4}{2} = \frac{z-5}{2}$ and the plane $x + y + z = 17$ is :
questions.explanation: A general point of the line is $(3 + t,\ 4 + 2t,\ 5 + 2t)$. Substituting in $x + y + z = 17$: $12 + 5t = 17 \Rightarrow t = 1$, so the point of intersection is $(4, 6, 7)$. Distance from $(1, 1, 9)$ $= \sqrt{9 + 25 + 4} = \sqrt{38}$.

questions.questionText: If the tangent to the curve $y = x^3$ at the point $P(t, t^3)$ meets the curve again at $Q$, then the ordinate of the point which divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $1 : 2$ is :
questions.explanation: Tangent at $P(t, t^3)$: $y - t^3 = 3t^2(x - t)$. With $y = x^3$: $x^3 - t^3 = 3t^2(x - t) \Rightarrow x^2 + xt - 2t^2 = 0$ (for $x \neq t$) $\Rightarrow (x - t)(x + 2t) = 0$, so $Q(-2t, -8t^3)$. The point dividing $PQ$ in $1 : 2$ has ordinate $\dfrac{2 \cdot t^3 + 1 \cdot (-8t^3)}{3} = -2t^3$.

questions.questionText: If $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\cos x - \sin x}{\sqrt{8 - \sin 2x}}\,dx = a\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sin x + \cos x}{b}\right) + c$, where $c$ is a constant of integration, then the ordered pair $(a, b)$ is equal to :
questions.explanation: $8 - \sin 2x = 9 - (\sin x + \cos x)^2$. Put $t = \sin x + \cos x$, $dt = (\cos x - \sin x)\,dx$: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{9 - t^2}} = \sin^{-1}\dfrac{t}{3} + c = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sin x + \cos x}{3}\right) + c$. So $a = 1,\ b = 3$.

questions.questionText: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{4x^3 - 3x^2}{6} - 2\sin x + (2x - 1)\cos x$ :
questions.explanation: $f'(x) = 2x^2 - x - 2\cos x + 2\cos x - (2x - 1)\sin x = (2x - 1)(x - \sin x)$. Since $x - \sin x > 0$ for $x > 0$ and $< 0$ for $x < 0$: $f'(x) \ge 0$ on $(-\infty, 0] \cup \left[\dfrac{1}{2}, \infty\right)$ and $f'(x) < 0$ on $\left(0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$. Hence $f$ increases in $\left[\dfrac{1}{2}, \infty\right)$.

questions.questionText: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined as $f(x) = 2x - 1$ and $g : \mathbb{R} - \{1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined as $g(x) = \dfrac{x - \frac{1}{2}}{x - 1}$. Then the composition function $f(g(x))$ is :
questions.explanation: $f(g(x)) = 2\cdot\dfrac{x - \frac{1}{2}}{x - 1} - 1 = \dfrac{2x - 1 - (x - 1)}{x - 1} = \dfrac{x}{x - 1} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{x - 1}$. This is one-one on $\mathbb{R} - \{1\}$, but its range is $\mathbb{R} - \{1\} \neq \mathbb{R}$, so it is one-one but not onto.

questions.questionText: An ordinary dice is rolled for a certain number of times. If the probability of getting an odd number 2 times is equal to the probability of getting an even number 3 times, then the probability of getting an odd number for odd number of times is :
questions.explanation: ${}^nC_2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^n = {}^nC_3\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^n \Rightarrow n = 5$. Required probability $= \left({}^5C_1 + {}^5C_3 + {}^5C_5\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^5 = \dfrac{5 + 10 + 1}{32} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.questionText: A scientific committee is to be formed from 6 Indians and 8 foreigners, which includes at least 2 Indians and double the number of foreigners as Indians. Then the number of ways, the committee can be formed, is :
The area (in sq. units) of the part of the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 36$, which is outside the parabola $y^2 = 9x$, is :
questions.explanation: The curves meet where $x^2 + 9x - 36 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 3$, $y = \pm 3\sqrt{3}$. Area inside both $= 2\left[\displaystyle\int_0^3 3\sqrt{x}\,dx + \int_3^6 \sqrt{36 - x^2}\,dx\right] = 2\left[6\sqrt{3} + \left(6\pi - \dfrac{9\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right] = 12\pi + 3\sqrt{3}$. Required area $= 36\pi - (12\pi + 3\sqrt{3}) = 24\pi - 3\sqrt{3}$.

questions.questionText: Let $p$ and $q$ be two positive numbers such that $p + q = 2$ and $p^4 + q^4 = 272$. Then $p$ and $q$ are roots of :
questions.explanation: $p^4 + q^4 = (p^2 + q^2)^2 - 2p^2q^2 = (4 - 2pq)^2 - 2p^2q^2 = 16 - 16pq + 2p^2q^2 = 272 \Rightarrow (pq)^2 - 8pq - 128 = 0 \Rightarrow pq = 16$ or $-8$. Taking $pq = 16$ (positive), the required equation is $x^2 - 2x + 16 = 0$.

questions.questionText: Two vertical poles are 150 m apart and the height of one is three times that of the other. If from the middle point of the line joining their feet, an observer finds the angles of elevation of their tops to be complementary, then the height of the shorter pole (in meters) is :
questions.explanation: Let the poles be $h$ and $3h$, each 75 m from the midpoint, with angles of elevation $\theta$ and $90^\circ - \theta$. Then $\tan\theta = \dfrac{h}{75}$ and $\cot\theta = \dfrac{3h}{75}$. Multiplying: $\dfrac{3h^2}{75^2} = 1 \Rightarrow h = \dfrac{75}{\sqrt{3}} = 25\sqrt{3}$ m.

questions.questionText: $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{\int_0^{x^2} \sin\sqrt{t}\,dt}{x^3}$ is equal to :
questions.explanation: Using L'Hospital's rule (Leibniz rule): $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{\sin\left(\sqrt{x^2}\right)\cdot 2x}{3x^2} = \lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{2}{3}\cdot\dfrac{\sin x}{x} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

questions.questionText: If $e^{(\cos^2 x + \cos^4 x + \cos^6 x + \dots)\ln 2}$ satisfies the equation $t^2 - 9t + 8 = 0$, then the value of $\frac{2\sin x}{\sin x + \sqrt{3}\cos x}$ for $0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2}$ is :
questions.explanation: For $0 < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$: $\cos^2 x + \cos^4 x + \dots = \dfrac{\cos^2 x}{1 - \cos^2 x} = \cot^2 x$, so the expression is $2^{\cot^2 x}$. Roots of $t^2 - 9t + 8 = 0$ are $1, 8$, so $\cot^2 x = 0$ or $3$; in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\cot x = \sqrt{3}$. Then $\dfrac{2\sin x}{\sin x + \sqrt{3}\cos x} = \dfrac{2}{1 + \sqrt{3}\cot x} = \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.questionText: The locus of the mid-point of the line segment joining the focus of the parabola $y^2 = 4ax$ to a moving point of the parabola, is another parabola whose directrix is :
questions.explanation: Focus $S(a, 0)$, point $P(at^2, 2at)$. Mid-point: $h = \dfrac{a(t^2 + 1)}{2}$, $k = at$. Eliminating $t$: $2h - a = \dfrac{k^2}{a}$, so the locus is $y^2 = a(2x - a) = 2a\left(x - \dfrac{a}{2}\right)$. Its vertex is $\left(\dfrac{a}{2}, 0\right)$ and $4A = 2a$, so the directrix is $x = \dfrac{a}{2} - \dfrac{a}{2} = 0$.

questions.questionText: If the least and the largest real values of $\alpha$, for which the equation $z + \alpha|z - 1| + 2i = 0$ ($z \in \mathbb{C}$ and $i = \sqrt{-1}$) has a solution, are $p$ and $q$ respectively, then $4(p^2 + q^2)$ is equal to _______.
questions.explanation: Let $z = x + iy$. Then $x + \alpha\sqrt{(x-1)^2 + y^2} + i(y + 2) = 0 \Rightarrow y = -2$ and $\alpha = \dfrac{-x}{\sqrt{x^2 - 2x + 5}}$. Now $\alpha^2 = \dfrac{x^2}{x^2 - 2x + 5}$ has maximum $\dfrac{5}{4}$ (at $x = 5$), so $\alpha \in \left[-\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}, \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\right]$. Hence $4(p^2 + q^2) = 4\left(\dfrac{5}{4} + \dfrac{5}{4}\right) = 10$.

questions.questionText: If $\int_{-a}^a (|x| + |x-2|)\,dx = 22, \ (a > 2)$ and $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer $\le x$, then $\int_{-a}^a (x + [x])\,dx$ is equal to _______.

Let $A = \{n \in \mathbb{N} : n \text{ is a 3-digit number}\}$, $B = \{9k + 2 : k \in \mathbb{N}\}$ and $C = \{9k + l : k \in \mathbb{N}\}$ for some $l\ (0 < l < 9)$. If the sum of all the elements of the set $A \cap (B \cup C)$ is $274 \times 400$, then $l$ is equal to ______.
questions.explanation: 3-digit members of $B$: $101, 110, \dots, 992$ (100 terms), sum $= \dfrac{100}{2}(101 + 992) = 54650$. If $l = 2$, $C = B$ and the sum would be $54650 \neq 109600$; so $l \neq 2$, $B \cap C = \phi$, and the sum of 3-digit members of $C$ is $109600 - 54650 = 54950$. These are $9k + l$ for $k = 11, \dots, 110$: sum $= 9\cdot\dfrac{100}{2}(11 + 110) + 100l = 54450 + 100l = 54950 \Rightarrow l = 5$.

questions.questionText: Let $M$ be any $3 \times 3$ matrix with entries from the set $\{0, 1, 2\}$. The maximum number of such matrices, for which the sum of diagonal elements of $M^TM$ is seven, is _______.
questions.explanation: $\text{tr}(M^TM)$ is the sum of squares of all nine entries, so we need $\sum a_{ij}^2 = 7$ with $a_{ij} \in \{0, 1, 2\}$. Case 1: seven 1's and two 0's: ${}^9C_2 = 36$. Case 2: one 2, three 1's, five 0's: $\dfrac{9!}{1!\,3!\,5!} = 504$. Total $= 540$.

questions.questionText: If one of the diameters of the circle $x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 6y + 6 = 0$ is a chord of another circle 'C', whose center is at $(2, 1)$, then its radius is ______ .
questions.explanation: The given circle has centre $(1, 3)$ and radius $\sqrt{1 + 9 - 6} = 2$. Its diameter is a chord of $C$, so the centre $(1, 3)$ is the midpoint of that chord. Distance between $(1, 3)$ and $(2, 1)$ is $\sqrt{5}$, hence $r^2 = (\sqrt{5})^2 + 2^2 = 9 \Rightarrow r = 3$.

questions.questionText: The minimum value of $\alpha$ for which the equation $\frac{4}{\sin x} + \frac{1}{1 - \sin x} = \alpha$ has at least one solution in $(0, \frac{\pi}{2})$ is _______.
questions.explanation: Let $s = \sin x \in (0, 1)$ and $f(s) = \dfrac{4}{s} + \dfrac{1}{1 - s}$. $f'(s) = -\dfrac{4}{s^2} + \dfrac{1}{(1 - s)^2} = 0 \Rightarrow 2(1 - s) = s \Rightarrow s = \dfrac{2}{3}$. $f_{\min} = 6 + 3 = 9$ and $f \to \infty$ at both ends, so by continuity the minimum $\alpha$ is $9$.

questions.questionText: $\lim_{n \to \infty} \tan\left(\sum_{r=1}^n \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1 + r + r^2}\right)\right)$ is equal to _______.
questions.explanation: $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{1 + r(r + 1)} = \tan^{-1}(r + 1) - \tan^{-1} r$. The sum telescopes to $\tan^{-1}(n + 1) - \dfrac{\pi}{4} \to \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$. Hence the limit is $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1$.

questions.questionText: Let three vectors $\vec a$, $\vec b$ and $\vec c$ be such that $\vec c$ is coplanar with $\vec a$ and $\vec b$, $\vec a \cdot \vec c = 7$ and $\vec b$ is perpendicular to $\vec c$, where $\vec a = -\hat i + \hat j + \hat k$ and $\vec b = 2\hat i + \hat k$, then the value of $2|\vec a + \vec b + \vec c|^2$ is ______.
questions.explanation: $\vec c$ is coplanar with $\vec a, \vec b$ and $\perp \vec b$, so $\vec c = \lambda\,\vec b \times (\vec a \times \vec b) = \lambda[(\vec b\cdot\vec b)\vec a - (\vec b\cdot\vec a)\vec b] = \lambda[5(-\hat i + \hat j + \hat k) + (2\hat i + \hat k)] = \lambda(-3\hat i + 5\hat j + 6\hat k)$. $\vec a\cdot\vec c = 14\lambda = 7 \Rightarrow \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$. Then $\vec a + \vec b + \vec c = -\dfrac{1}{2}\hat i + \dfrac{7}{2}\hat j + 5\hat k$, so $2|\vec a + \vec b + \vec c|^2 = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{49}{4} + 25\right) = 75$.

questions.questionText: Let $B_i\ (i = 1, 2, 3)$ be three independent events in a sample space. The probability that only $B_1$ occurs is $\alpha$, only $B_2$ occurs is $\beta$ and only $B_3$ occurs is $\gamma$. Let $p$ be the probability that none of the events $B_i$ occurs and these 4 probabilities satisfy the equations $(\alpha - 2\beta)p = \alpha\beta$ and $(\beta - 3\gamma)p = 2\beta\gamma$ (All the probabilities are assumed to lie in the interval $(0, 1)$). Then $\dfrac{P(B_1)}{P(B_3)}$ is equal to ______.
questions.explanation: Let $P(B_i) = p_i$. Then $\dfrac{\alpha}{p} = \dfrac{p_1}{1 - p_1} = x_1$, $\dfrac{\beta}{p} = x_2$, $\dfrac{\gamma}{p} = x_3$ (with $x_i = \dfrac{p_i}{1 - p_i}$). The conditions become $x_1 - 2x_2 = x_1x_2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{x_2} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{x_1}$ and $x_2 - 3x_3 = 2x_2x_3 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{x_3} = 2 + \dfrac{3}{x_2} = 5 + \dfrac{6}{x_1}$. Since $\dfrac{1}{x_i} = \dfrac{1}{p_i} - 1$: $\dfrac{1}{p_3} - 1 = 5 + \dfrac{6}{p_1} - 6 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{p_3} = \dfrac{6}{p_1} \Rightarrow \dfrac{P(B_1)}{P(B_3)} = 6$.

questions.questionText: Let $P = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & \alpha \\ 3 & -5 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, where $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Suppose $Q = [q_{ij}]$ is a matrix satisfying $PQ = kI_3$ for some non-zero $k \in \mathbb{R}$. If $q_{23} = -\dfrac{k}{8}$ and $|Q| = \dfrac{k^2}{2}$, then $\alpha^2 + k^2$ is equal to _______.
questions.explanation: $|P| = 3(5\alpha) + 1(-3\alpha) - 2(-10) = 12\alpha + 20$, and $Q = kP^{-1} = \dfrac{k}{|P|}\,\text{adj}\,P$. $q_{23} = \dfrac{k}{|P|}C_{32} = \dfrac{-k(3\alpha + 4)}{|P|} = -\dfrac{k}{8} \Rightarrow 12\alpha + 20 = 8(3\alpha + 4) \Rightarrow \alpha = -1$, $|P| = 8$. Also $|P||Q| = k^3 \Rightarrow 8\cdot\dfrac{k^2}{2} = k^3 \Rightarrow k = 4$. Hence $\alpha^2 + k^2 = 1 + 16 = 17$.
